'''Adolph Ludvig Otto Jensen''' (15 July 1866 – 24 May 1948) was an economist and statistician of international standing, and from 1913 to 1936 the head of the Statistics Department of the [[Ministry of Finance (Denmark)|Danish Ministry of Finance]].<ref name=obit>Obituary by H. Kofoed and E. Cohn in ''Nationaløkonomisk Tidsskrift'', 1948–49, pp.&nbsp;81–87.</ref>

==Career==
Jensen studied Politics at [[Århus University]], 1885–1892, under [[Harald Westergaard]].<ref name=obit/> From 1896 to 1936, he worked at the Department of Statistics of the Danish Ministry of Finance, becoming head of the department in 1913.<ref name=obit/> He took an active part in international research into statistics, as well as statistical research into economic and social issues.

==Publications==
*The chapter on "The Scandinavian Nations" in volume 4 of ''[[A History of Banking in all the Leading Nations]]'' (1896; reprinted 1971).
*"The History and Development of Statistics in Denmark", in ''The History of Statistics'', collected and edited by John Koren (Published for the [[American Statistical Association]] by the [[Macmillan Company]] of New York, 1918), pp.&nbsp;201–214.<ref>[https://archive.org/details/cu31924013894997 Available] from the [[Internet Archive]].</ref>
*"Report on the Representative Method in Statistics", ''[[Bulletin de l'Institut International de Statistique]]'' 22 (1925), 359–380
*"Purposive Selection", ''[[Journal of the Royal Statistical Society]]'' 91:4 (1928), 541–547.
*"Horoscope of the Population of Denmark", ''Bulletin de l'Institut International de Statistique'', 25 (1931), 41–49.
*"Migration Statistics of Denmark, Norway and Sweden", in ''International Migrations, Volume II: Interpretations'', ed. Walter F. Willcox, National Bureau of Economic Research, 1931.
*''Befolkningsspørgsmaalet i Danmark'', 1939.
*''Tallenes Tale'', 1941.
